author: n. h. coburn
title: Live Oak Elementary School reports 673 African American students enrolled for 2024-25
text:
In the 2024-25 school year, Live Oak Elementary School had 673 African American students enrolled, representing an 11.6% increase over the prior year, the Georgia Department of Education reported.
According to data, the school’s total enrollment reached 740 students in 2024-25. African American students represented 91% of the student body, making them the predominant demographic group at the school.
Located in the Dougherty County School District, Live Oak Elementary School’s district administrative office is in Albany.
Of the 21 schools in the Dougherty County School District, Westover High School posted the highest number of African American student enrollments for the 2024-25 school year at 1,118 students.
Statistics from the National Center for Education Statistics show public school demographics in Georgia at about 36.4% Black, 35.9% white, 18.1% Hispanic, 4% Asian, 4.6% multiracial, 0.2% American Indian or Alaska Native, and 0.1% Pacific Islander.
Chronic absenteeism remains a significant issue across Georgia’s schools, with 20.7% of students reported to have missed 10% or more of classes in 2024, according to the Georgia Department of Education. In response, GaDOE has initiated statewide efforts involving a real-time attendance dashboard, awareness campaigns, and additional support for districts with higher needs to promote student attendance.
Georgia lawmakers passed a bill in 2025 that updates attendance rules by banning student expulsions for absenteeism alone. The legislation also requires enhanced reporting and supports alternative routes to diploma attainment for students.
As of 2026, Georgia’s average student-to-teacher ratio was about 14:1 , lower than the national average of 15:1 .
